mechanism_narrative: A 2% quarterly increase in GDP (GDPC1) indicates strengthening economic demand, leading to increased consumer spending and, subsequently, positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in > 50% of quarters with GDPC1 growth > 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) signals accommodative monetary policy, supporting positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 1.5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment (UNRATE) falls below 5%, labor market tightness leads to increased wage pressure, driving inflation expectations and, subsequently, negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances with UNRATE < 5%.

mechanism_narrative: Interaction between increasing industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates a supply-side boom, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward correlation between INDPRO, HOUST, and SPX returns remains below 0.1 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A 5% monthly increase in retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, but only during the holiday season (Nov-Jan).
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of holiday seasons with RSAFS growth > 5%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds the CPI inflation rate (CPIAUCSL), real interest rates turn positive, signaling a monetary tightening cycle that leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward correlation between FEDFUNDS-CPIAUCSL spread and SPX returns remains above -0.1 over any 1.5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Always-on signal: positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days due to the consistent, long-term growth in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS).
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.01 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Interaction between decreasing industrial production (INDPRO) and increasing unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a supply-side downturn, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, but only during recessions.
failure_condition: Walk-forward correlation between INDPRO, UNRATE, and SPX returns remains above -0.2 over any 1.5-year rolling window during recessions.
